messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finlytics.com>, Samantha Rhee <samantha@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo recap — tactical model shortlist & go/no-go signals

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the clarity on your latency targets and the hallucination examples you surfaced. Quick written recap and tactical asks so we can move from demo -> pilot.

1) Shortlist (recommended for pilot) — reasoned picks and tradeoffs:
- redwood/compact-1.7q (quantized): best cost profile for high throughput; p95 latency ~85ms at 512 token window; slightly lower factuality on edge-case finance queries but easy to harden with data-augmentation + prompt engineering.
- open/llama3-13b-q4: balanced quality/latency; p95 ~140ms; stronger on instruction-following and fewer hallucinations in our evals; cost ~1.7x compact.
- redwood/econ-2.9 (2.9B econ-tuned): best out-of-the-box financial Q&A quality; p95 ~220ms; higher cost but shows lowest regression risk on your prompt set.

Rationale in bullets: compact for throughput/cost, llama3 for balanced quality and predictable latency, econ-2.9 for highest accuracy on nuance. We recommend running the three-way pilot with golden prompts + regression harness.

2) Benchmarks & artifacts I attached/linked:
- Prompt pack (attached): finlytics_demo_prompt_pack_v1.zip — contains 120 example prompts, edge-case hallucination probes, and suggested guardrail templates.
- Perf dashboard: https://redwood-inference.internal/perf/finlytics/20260519 — contains the raw p50/p95/p99 traces for the three candidates across token-length buckets.
- Eval notebook & metrics (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_prompt_pack_finlytics

3) Risk & regression plan (short):
- Run a 48-hour regression sweep on the 120 prompts against each candidate; track hallucination rate (binary), factuality score (0-1), and latency percentiles by sequence length.
- If econ-2.9 is within 10% of llama3 on latency when pinned to a 512 token window, prioritize it for the pilot.

4) Asks / next steps for FinLytics:
- Go/no-go signal on pilot slate by EOD Friday (May 21) — which candidate(s) you want included.
- Procurement contact (we'll push a scoped SOW) — CC procurement@finlytics.com if you want us to loop them in.
- Any additional eval prompts you'd like added to the pack (we can integrate up to 40 more).

If you prefer, we can also do a short follow-up focused only on hallucination probes (30min).

Thanks — will queue Ben/Karthik to provision the pilot if we get a go.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Liam — quick results from the targeted re-runs using your prompt pack (attached CSV + summary):

Executive numbers (2k token bucket, p95):
- redwood/compact-1.7q: p95 = 420ms (note: compact's latency increases non-linearly past 1k tokens in our setup)
- open/llama3-13b-q4: p95 = 320ms
- redwood/econ-2.9: p95 = 360ms (with quantization disabled; with q4 it jumps to ~520ms)

Cost (rough, hosted rate equivalent):
- compact-1.7q: $0.008 per 1k tokens
- llama3-13b-q4: $0.014 per 1k tokens
- econ-2.9: $0.022 per 1k tokens

Quality notes from the 120-prompt sweep (summary):
- econ-2.9 reduced hallucination binary rate by ~22% vs compact and ~9% vs llama3 on finance-specific probes (we flagged samples in the CSV).
- llama3 had the best middle-ground for instruction-following and fewer formatting failures in table outputs.
- compact produced the most throughput but missed subtle currency-normalization cases unless paired with a brief post-processing step.

Attachments included: benchmarks_finlytics_20260519.csv (rows: prompt_id, model, tokens, p50, p95, p99, hallucination_flag, factuality_score), short annotated samples folder in Drive.

Recommended pilot framing (tactical):
- Pilot A: compact + guardrails (post-processing) — low-cost throughput path; test with 48-hour production shadowing at 10% traffic.
- Pilot B: llama3-13b-q4 — balanced path, run A/B for 7 days against compact to measure delta in end-user task success (we can track your CSAT metric).
- Pilot C: econ-2.9 (select prompts) — only route highly sensitive queries to econ-2.9 via rule routing; reduces spend while targeting accuracy.

Regression guardrails proposal (deliverable within 5 business days if you sign pilot):
- We run the full 120 prompt sweep nightly for 7 nights; we track hallucination rate, factuality delta, latency p95; alert if hallucination increases >5% from baseline.
- If OK, we'll include an automated fallback to llama3 for prompts that show >0.6 hallucination score over a 24h window.

Procurement/SOW notes: I attached a draft SOW (SOW_finlytics_v1.docx) with scoped pilot terms (30-day pilot, credit cap). For quick review: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-8432 (internal). DocuSign link available once you sign the SOW.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the CSV and the annotated examples.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmarks_finlytics_20260519.csv, SOW_finlytics_v1.docx
